The first atomic weapon to be used in warfare dropped silently for 43 seconds, with a parachute billowing behind slowing its descent enough to allow Tibbets and his crew to escape the ensuing explosion. At approximately 1,890feet above the Japanese city of Hiroshima it detonated, unleashing a blinding flash and a force of unprecedented magnitude. The temperature at Ground Zero was estimated to be several thousand degrees, approximately the surface temperature of the sun.
